column1: What is a vertex and what is an edge?
column2: A vertex is a dot (a service, a region). An edge is a line between two dots. A directed edge is an arrow.

column1: Adjacency list versus adjacency matrix: memory cost?
column2: List: grows with \(|V| + |E|\). Matrix: grows with \(|V|^2\). Sparse graphs (most real ones) favor the list.
A list of all vertices where, for each arrow \(A \to B\) meaning A needs B, B comes first. A safe start order. It exists exactly when the graph has no cycle.
Queue every vertex with zero unmet dependencies, pop one, decrement its dependents, enqueue any that hit zero, repeat.

column1: How does Kahn reveal a cycle?
column2: The queue empties before every vertex is placed. Order length < \(|V|\) means a cycle exists.
WHITE: not seen. GRAY: on the current walk. BLACK: finished. An arrow into a GRAY vertex (a back edge) closes a cycle.

column1: Why does Dijkstra need non-negative weights?
column2: It finishes vertices in order of distance. A negative edge lets a later detour come out shorter, which breaks that order.

column1: When is BFS enough for shortest paths?
column2: When every edge counts the same (hop count). BFS visits vertices in rings of 0, 1, 2 hops.

column1: us-east to ap-south: fewest hops versus lowest latency in the workshop?
column2: Direct link: 1 hop, 230 ms. Via eu-west: 2 hops, 75 + 120 = 195 ms.

column1: What is the blast radius of service x?
column2: Every service with a path of dependency arrows to x. Compute it with BFS on reversed edges.

column1: Why is in-degree not the whole risk picture?
column2: It counts only direct dependents. config has in-degree 1 but a blast radius of 4 because it sits under auth, which sits under api.
A vertex whose removal splits a two-way graph into separate pieces. A single point of failure in the topology.

column1: Tarjan test for a non-root cut vertex u?
column2: Some DFS child v has \(\text{low}(v) \ge \text{disc}(u)\): nothing below v has a way around u.
